images.name: Knots tied and untied
images.source: chain map: Binding, Fulfillment, and Release; chain map: Obligation as a Tied Structure; chain map: Lawful Release Without Rupture
images.scene: A cord is twisted and knotted: the believers are told to keep every knot whole. God then loosens some knots (the herd, game after leaving ihram, the food of the People of the Book) and leaves others tight (the pilgrim's state, God's marks). At the end the whole bundle turns out to be one bond with which God has tied the believers to Himself.

images.containment: 'Fulfil the contracts' stays a command to keep one's agreements, and it can also be heard as keeping every knot tied until the One who tied it loosens it.
images.perceptible: The ruling words become one physical act seen from two sides: halal is a knot God has opened, haram and ihram are knots still tied. A Turkish reader for whom 'helal' and 'haram' are two labels sees them as tension and slack on one cord. Leaving ihram (حللتم) is literally the pilgrim untying himself, and the covenant of 5:7 turns out to be the cord that holds all the rulings together.

interactions.how: The twisted cord (ق ل د B001) is the same cord that hangs on the sacrificial animal's neck as a marker, so the image of tying is shown on a body.
أوفوا is both keeping the knot and giving the full measure. The bond is kept whole in the same act by which things are brought to completion.
Illicit intercourse is classically defined as pouring out water without a knot (سفاح بلا عقد). The marriage enclosure is a knot, and its absence is spillage.

images.movement: Opens the window: the whole passage is a list of which knots are tied and which are loosened. It closes in 5:7, where the knots turn out to be one covenant the believers once tied themselves by saying 'we heard and we obeyed'.

images.name: The animal's end: whose mark, whose name, whose hand
images.source: chain map: Boundary Marks and Visible Restraint; chain map: The Marked Offering; chain map: Competing Modes of Death; chain map: A Bloodied Standing Stone Redirects Slaughter
images.scene: Two animals. One carries God's mark: a twisted cord on its neck, led as an offering to the sanctuary, its life ended by a complete cut at the throat with God's name spoken over it. The other's neck is squeezed by a choking cord, or it is clubbed, falls from a height, is gored, or is eaten by a wild beast. Or its blood runs on an erected stone while another name is shouted, and its meat is shared out by arrows.

images.containment: The list stays a list of forbidden meats, and it can also be heard as a question about whose mark and whose name are on an animal's neck at the moment its life ends.
images.perceptible: The prohibitions in 5:3 stop reading as an arbitrary menu and become a contrast of necks: the neck with God's cord (قلائد) against the neck with a choking collar (مخنقة is attested for both a strangling and a necklace). The throat opened in God's name stands against blood poured on a stone to another name. Lawful meat is a matter of who ends the life and in whose name, and the name spoken in 5:4 is heard as a brand (وسم).

interactions.how: The cord of binding and the cord on the neck are one cord (ق ل د B001/B002). Undoing God's marks (لا تحلوا شعائر الله) is untying that cord.

ذكاة is attested as completion of the slaughter. The same ayah moves from the completed cut to God completing the religion, and pits the arrow-lots that complete shares of meat (تتميم الأيسار) against God's own completing.
The wild beast (سبع) that eats for itself in 5:3 is answered by the trained hunter that holds its catch for you in 5:4. The difference is who the killing is for.

images.movement: Opens in 5:2 with the marked offering on its way to the House, becomes explicit in 5:3's catalogue of wrong ends, and closes in 5:4 when God's name is spoken over what the trained animals caught: the lawful is what bears His mark.

images.name: Full measure: the blessing completed
images.source: chain map: Obligation as a Tied Structure; new
images.scene: A herd is given, and a slaughtered beast is divided into portions. The pagans fill up each man's share by drawing arrows. God instead fills up the measure Himself: He completes the religion and the blessing, meets the starving man's empty belly, and makes little enough (clean earth for water), so that the blessing reaches its full term.

images.containment: 'Today I have completed your religion' keeps its plain sense, and in its own ayah it can also be heard against the pagan filling of meat-shares by arrows: God, not the lot, fills the measure.
images.perceptible: The same verse forbids dividing meat by arrows and declares the religion completed, and ت م م attests 'completing the shares' in that very game. What looks like two unrelated statements becomes one scene of portions and fullness. The livestock (أنعام) of 5:1 and the blessing (نعمة) of 5:3, 5:6, 5:7 and 5:11 are one root: the blessing first arrives as a herd.

interactions.how: The completed cut (ذكاة) and the completed religion stand in one ayah. The arrow-lots belong to both images.
ليتم نعمته closes the purification ayah: the blessing reaches the body through water, or through earth when water is missing.
أوفوا is the human side of completion: the believer gives the full measure, and God completes the blessing.

images.movement: Runs from 5:1 (fulfil in full, the herd given) through the centre of 5:3 to 5:6 (so that He may complete His blessing). The rulings are the form a completed blessing takes.

images.name: Grip and restraint: the hunter's hand held back
images.source: chain map: Captured Life and the Threshold of Edibility; chain map: The Trained Predator Holds for Another; chain map: The Withheld Hand; chain map: Sanctuary as Held Conduct
images.scene: A chase. The pilgrim's hand is held back from the game while he is in ihram and released when he leaves it. The wild beast seizes and eats for itself. The trained hawk or hound, taught by men whom God taught, seizes and then holds the catch for its master without eating. At the end the believers are the quarry: a people stretch out their hands toward them, and God holds those hands back.

images.containment: The hunting rules and the reminder in 5:11 keep their plain sense, and together they can be heard as one chase in which the believers first learn to hold back their own grip and then find God holding back the grip reaching for them.
images.perceptible: It makes perceptible why the hunting rules and 5:11 belong together. Ihram trains the hand to stop; the trained hound shows that a grip can hold without devouring (أمسكن عليكم). In 5:11 the believers who were taught to restrain their reach are themselves the quarry, and God does to the hostile hand what they did to their own. كفّ is both 'palm' and 'hold back': the hand is stopped in its own organ.

interactions.how: جوارح are named because they 'earn' for their masters. The same hunting grip is the image of earning.
The chase after game (ع د و B008) and the transgression against people (ع د و B001) are one word in 5:2. Justice is the hunter's restraint turned toward human enemies.
The wild beast's kill is forbidden and the trained beast's held catch is lawful once God's name is spoken over it.

images.movement: Opens in 5:1 with game forbidden during ihram, is released in 5:2, is trained in 5:4, and turns around in 5:11, where the believers are the prey and God is the restrainer. The window ends in trust (توكل).

images.name: What the hands earn and where it ends
images.scene: Hunting animals wound and 'earn' for their owners. Hatred tries to make the believers 'earn' a crime. A man pays the wage owed to a bride. Work swells and dies like an animal that has grazed on poisonous pasture. A trader comes out at a loss. The final account brings a great wage or company in the blaze.

images.containment: 'Let not hatred of a people move you to transgress' keeps its plain sense, and it can also be heard as: do not let hatred be the hunting hound that earns a crime for you.
images.perceptible: The verb in لا يجرمنكم is heard, as classical glosses have it, as 'make you earn', and the hunting beasts of 5:4 are called جوارح because they earn. So the forbidden transgression becomes a catch brought in by the wrong hound. حبط (bloating from poisonous pasture) makes the voided work bodily: in a passage about what may be eaten, the rejecter's deeds swell and die like a beast that grazed badly.

interactions.how: The hunting grip is the model of earning. What you train decides what is brought to you.
Hatred is the weight on the scale and also the agent that would make the believers earn injustice.
The bride's wage (أجور) is earning handed over in the right way, set against spillage without a bond.

images.movement: Runs underneath the rulings from 5:2 to 5:10 and gathers them into their end: whatever the hands, beasts and hatreds 'earn' is tallied quickly (سريع الحساب) and becomes either a great wage or the blaze.

images.name: Protected precincts: the sacred House and the fortified household
images.source: chain map: Intimacy as Fortification or Spillage; chain map: Marriage Builds an Enclosure; chain map: Uncontained and Secret Access; chain map: A Wedding Moves From Contract to Household; chain map: Sanctuary as Held Conduct
images.scene: A walled sanctuary, the House, which pilgrims head for with offerings and which enemies once barred them from. A fortress whose inside cannot be reached, which is how chaste and married women are described. It is entered through the gate of a contract and a paid bride-wage, like a bride led to her husband's house. Outside, water is spilled with no contract, or a secret companion is kept.

intercourse with no contract, 'pouring water without a knot'
the secret companion of desire, a hidden door

images.containment: The permission to marry chaste women stays a ruling on marriage, and it can also be heard as building a second protected precinct, a household entered only through contract and bride-wage just as the House is entered in a state of sanctity.
images.perceptible: The reader can see why marriage law sits beside pilgrimage law. Both are enclosures with a lawful gate. محصنة is literally a fortified place, and سفاح is water spilled with no knot, which ties marriage back to the 'contracts' of 5:1. The offering led to the House and the bride led to her husband share one word (هدي/هدى).

interactions.how: The fortress is entered by a knot (contract). Spillage is the knot's absence.
The bride-wage is a rightful handing-over of earnings at the gate.
Poured-out water (سفاح) against water that purifies (5:6): the same element spilled or used for cleansing.

images.movement: The sanctuary of 5:2 prepares the household of 5:5. The passage protects two precincts, God's House and the believer's house, and in both the permitted comes in through a lawful opening.

images.name: Water and clean earth over the body
images.source: chain map: Purification Across Material Surfaces; chain map: Washing With Flowing Water; chain map: Clean Earth as a Transfer Medium
images.scene: A person rises for prayer and passes water over the face, over the arms up to the elbows, over the head with a light wipe, and over the feet to the ankle-bones. After major impurity, after coming back from the low ground, or after touching a woman, if no water is found they head for clean high-lying earth and pass it over face and hands. They are not forced into a narrow thicket; the same act carries them out.

images.containment: Tayammum stays the ruling of dry ablution, and it can also be heard as heading for the earth's clean face when the great water is missing, and finding that it still carries one out of the narrow place.
images.perceptible: The limbs become a map with limits (elbow, ankle-bone), and the two media, flowing water and the earth's face, do the same work of carrying away. تيمم, whose root also names the sea, is the gesture of heading for the substitute, like the pilgrims 'heading for' the House in 5:2. The low ground (غائط) and the high clean earth (صعيد) turn purification into a movement from low to high. The Turkish loanword 'teyemmüm', narrowed to a technical rite, gets back its motion of intent.

interactions.how: The ayah ends with purification as the way God completes His blessing on the body.
Water poured out without a bond (سفاح) against water and earth that purify.
The permission of tayammum is a knot loosened for the traveller and the sick; ح ر ج also attests prohibition (B004), and God denies imposing it.

images.movement: Moves from what enters the body (food, 5:3-5) to what passes over its surface (5:6). The same logic holds: the permitted is given widely and constriction is removed so that the blessing reaches completion.

images.name: The level scale under hatred's weight
images.source: chain map: Justice Arrests Hostile Motion; chain map: Testimony Held to an Even Line
images.scene: A balance, or a camel load divided into two matched sides. Hatred of a people presses down one side and tempts the carrier to lean and to run past the limit. The believers stand up straight, holding the beam level as witnesses, and they lean toward nothing, not even toward sin when hunger forces them.

leaning away from the straight line
standing upright, the beam straight
the one who keeps the thing standing and gives it its due
the witness who makes the matter clear
the straight balance
equity itself
the load matched against its counter-load
justice in judgement
nearness: the level beam is closest to taqwa

images.containment: 'Be upright for God, witnesses in justice' keeps its plain sense, and it can also be heard as holding a scale or a two-sided load level while hatred pushes down one side.
images.perceptible: عدل is a load balanced against a load, قسط is the straight balance, and جنف is leaning. So justice toward enemies becomes a bodily balancing act, not an abstract virtue: the witness stands upright (قوّام) with hatred's weight on one side and keeps the beam level. The same prohibition in 5:2 (not to overstep) and 5:8 (not to lean) are two failures of one balance.

interactions.how: Transgression (اعتداء) shares its word with the hunter's run from kill to kill. Justice is restraint of the chase.
Hatred is also the hound that would earn a crime for them (يجرمنكم).
Keeping the balance toward those who barred them from the sanctuary is itself fulfilling the covenant recalled in 5:7.

images.movement: Opens in 5:2 (those who barred you from the Mosque), passes through 5:3 (not leaning toward sin even in hunger), and comes to rest in 5:8, where the covenant people are called to be the level beam. It prepares 5:11, where the enemy's hand is stopped by God, not by the believers' excess.

concepts.concept: Loosening what was bound, so that a thing may be used or a place settled in: permission is an untied knot.
A withheld zone that protects: forbidden things, the sacred precinct, the pilgrim's state, the sacred month and inviolable rights are all one enclosure that must not be broken into.
Blessing as a good, soft life that first appears as the herd: the livestock of 5:1 and the blessing completed in 5:3 are one gift.
What the self finds wholesome and clean: good food, 'the two good things' of eating and marriage (5:4-5), and clean earth that removes filth (5:6).
Reaching full measure: the blessing completed, the term reached, and the shares of the slaughtered camel filled in, which God's completion replaces.
The gash that gains: wounding, earning, and the hunting beasts that earn by wounding for their masters.
An enclosure no one can reach into: fortress, chastity, the protection of marriage, and the stallion that guards its rider.
Matching one side against the other: justice, equivalence, and the camel load balanced by its counter-load.
Tying ends so that they hold: the knot, the contract, and the heart set firm on something.
The palm and its closing: the organ that grasps is also the act of holding back.

structured_output.movement: The window opens with one command, keep the knots, and then shows which knots God has untied (the herd, game after ihram, good food, chaste women through contract) and which stay tied (the pilgrim's state, God's marks on the offering, the sanctuary, justice toward enemies). At its centre, 5:3 sets the necks of animals, marked and named for God or choked and bled on a stone, against God's own act of completion: the religion and the blessing brought to full measure in the same breath that bans dividing meat by arrows. The blessing then reaches the body's surface through water or clean earth, without constriction (5:6). The covenant is revealed as the single cord behind every ruling (5:7), and the believers must keep the scale level against the weight of hatred (5:8). Whatever hands, hounds and hatreds 'earn' ends in wage or blaze (5:9-10). In the last ayah the hunters who learned to restrain their grip become the quarry, and God stops the hands stretched toward them. The restraint they practised is returned to them as protection, and the window ends in trust.

plan.note: Make the knot audible in عقود/أحلت: halal as a knot God has opened, ihram as a knot still tied on the hunter's hand. Note that the herd (أنعام) shares its root with the blessing (نعمة) that returns in 5:3.

Show the offering with its twisted cord on the neck, the pilgrim untying himself (حللتم), and the first appearance of hatred as a weight that pushes one past the limit (تعتدوا), a word that also names the hunter's run from kill to kill.

Show the necks side by side: God's cord against the choking collar (مخنقة), the completed cut against the stone and the arrows. Let 'I have completed' be heard against the arrow-game's 'completing the shares', and keep the hungry man who does not lean (متجانف).
The trained hound holds its catch for you (أمسكن عليكم) where the wild beast ate for itself. جوارح are named as 'earners'. God's name spoken over the catch is heard as a brand that makes it His.

Food and marriage, 'the two good things', are released together. The chaste woman is a fortress entered through contract and bride-wage, like the House; spillage is water without a knot. Void works swell and die like a beast that grazed on harmful pasture (حبط).

Trace the limbs and their limits, the move from low ground (غائط) to the earth's clean face (صعيد), and tayammum as heading for the substitute when the great water is missing. Constriction (حرج) is lifted so that the blessing reaches its full measure.
All the knots of 5:1 turn out to be one cord: the covenant God tied with the believers when they said 'we heard and obeyed'. Remembering the blessing means remembering the bond.
The witness stands upright holding a level beam, a load matched by its counter-load (عدل). Hatred presses one side and would 'earn' injustice for them; being level is nearest to taqwa.
The earning ends in forgiveness, which covers, and a great wage: what the hands earned rightly is paid out in full.
The other end of earning: those who covered up and denied become companions of the blaze, the opposite outcome to the wage in 5:9.

The hunters become the quarry: hands stretched toward the believers are folded back by God (كفّ is palm and restraint at once). The restraint they learned in ihram and in training hounds is returned to them as protection, and they entrust themselves to Him.

chains_set_aside.title: S14. A Bow Is Finished and Stress-Tested
chains_set_aside.why: Its only member here is م س ح B013 (the smoothed bow). The wiping in 5:6 is of one's own face and limbs, and nothing in this window activates a bow.

chains_set_aside.title: S15. Seed Is Covered, Raised, and Ripened
chains_set_aside.why: ك ف ر B008 and ش ك ر B004 are not activated here. The window has no soil, sowing or crop context; the earth in 5:6 is a cleansing surface, not farmland.

chains_set_aside.title: S16. A Waterskin Is Stitched Leak-Tight
chains_set_aside.why: ك ل ب B006 and م س ك B005 are overridden by the hunting scene in 5:4, which the ayah's own words (جوارح, مكلبين, أمسكن) activate. Nothing points to leatherwork.

chains_set_aside.title: S17. A Reservoir Directs and Retains Water
chains_set_aside.why: The members (أجور, ء ت ي B004, م س ك B004) are scattered across unrelated ayat. The only water here is purification water in 5:6, which I7 covers.

chains_set_aside.title: S18. Milk Is Collected, Set, and Thickened
chains_set_aside.why: ق ل د B008, ك ع ب B006 and ر ب ب B006 have no activating context. The قلائد are neck-cords and the كعبان are ankle-bones.

chains_set_aside.title: S19. A Herd Takes Its Appointed Watering Turn
chains_set_aside.why: ق ل د B007 and ق ب ل B014 are not activated in this window. Whatever payoff it has lies in far ayat.

chains_set_aside.title: S20. Sorcery Works Through Knots and Diversion
chains_set_aside.why: ع ق د B013 is heard only if 5:1 is read against 5:110. The divining arrows in 5:3 are lots, not knots, and are kept in I2/I3 instead.

chains_set_aside.title: S21. A Sale Is Ratified Palm to Palm
chains_set_aside.why: The wiping in 5:6 is of one's own face and hands, and لامستم is glossed as touching/intercourse. The handshake of a sale is not activated here.

chains_set_aside.title: S26. A Padded Garment Is Cut, Filled, and Hemmed
chains_set_aside.why: ك ف ف B004 (hem) and ق س م B007 are overridden by restraint in 5:11 and lot-taking in 5:3.

chains_set_aside.title: S30. A Weak-Hocked Mount Cuts Off the Journey
chains_set_aside.why: ح ل ل B014 and و ك ل B005 have no activating context. The traveller in 5:6 is excused, not stranded by a mount.

chains_set_aside.title: S32. Rain Descends, Travels, and Revives Ground
chains_set_aside.why: No member in this window carries rain. ء ت ي B005 in أوتوا is inert here.

chains_set_aside.title: S33. A Hearth Pot Is Supported, Lowered, and Strained
chains_set_aside.why: ج ع ل B007 (the cloth for lowering a pot) in 5:6 has no cooking context around it.

5:2:41 و ق ي B001 (a shield): taqwa, repeated in almost every ayah, as the protective covering, activated by the dangers of the hunt and of enemies.
